custom-instructions-architect.md.scenario: A senior financial-crime analyst has the assistant write an optimized ChatGPT custom-instructions block so every future chat starts already tuned to their voice and constraints.
fills: your role, seniority, field
Senior financial-crime compliance analyst at a large bank; I use an AI assistant daily for research, drafting memos, screening entities, and reviewing documents.
the subject areas you work in
AML/CFT, sanctions, crypto and digital-asset compliance, regulatory analysis. Assume expert level and do not explain the basics.
the handful of things
Draft audit-defensible memos, compare options in tables, summarize long documents, screen entities, and translate regulation into structured obligations.
tone, format defaults
Lead with the answer; dense and direct, no filler; tables for any comparison of three or more items; cite sources; no marketing language; never use emojis.
anything the assistant must always or never do
Never fabricate a citation; treat vendor claims as unverified until corroborated; keep outputs generic and public-source only; always flag a confidence level.
where this will live
ChatGPT custom instructions — the two boxes ('what should the assistant know about you' and 'how should it respond'), roughly a 1,500-character budget each.
paste anything that reveals your preferences
A sample I liked: a tight severity-tagged risk memo that led with the disposition. A sample I disliked: a hedge-heavy, emoji-laden summary that buried the answer.
paste your current custom-instructions block
Current block: 'Be concise and professional. Help me with compliance tasks.' — too vague; re-tune it.

outlook-copilot-automation.md.scenario: A compliance analyst has the assistant design an Outlook rule/category scheme and a Copilot triage routine that surfaces client deadlines buried under alert emails, without ever deleting or sending mail.
fills: your role and what your inbox is mostly full of
Compliance analyst. My inbox is mostly internal case threads, external client requests, automated alert emails, and vendor newsletters.
the senders, topics, and deadlines
My manager and the MLRO; anything with 'SAR', 'deadline', or 'exam' in the subject; and a named set of priority clients.
what clutters the inbox
High-volume automated alert emails and newsletters bury client deadlines, and I re-read the same long threads to find the actual ask.
folders, categories, or rules already in place
One 'Clients' folder and two color categories (Red = urgent, Blue = FYI). No rules configured yet.
anything that must hold
Records retention: nothing may be auto-deleted, regulated mail must stay in the mailbox, and no mail may be auto-forwarded externally.
what you can use
Outlook plus Microsoft 365 Copilot, on desktop and mobile.
paste a sample of real subject lines

Sample subjects/senders: 'ALERT: rule TM-14 triggered' (monitoring-system), 'Re: Q1 review deadline Friday' (manager), 'Weekly AML newsletter' (vendor), 'Client Aurora — urgent RFI' (relationship manager), 'Exam prep — evidence request' (MLRO).
paste a previous design
None — first design. Baseline.
